 Rewards! November Live Trading Streak Challenge: Win Up Yo 50,000 Points* 304K Views · 938 Posts tey7437 joined discussion · 17:14 NOV check in #7
 NVIDIA is down about 1.1% in pre-market at around 197.9, after closing near 200. This is the monthly chart, and the long-term trend is still strongly up, with price far above every major moving average. But the last two monthly candles are red, and the stock has pulled back about 18% from its high near 243. That makes it a cooling-off phase, not a clean trend continuation yet. I'm not chasing this weakness, and I'm not selling the long-term trend either. My plan is to hold my core position and add only if price pulls back toward the 180 area, where the short-term monthly average sits. I'd keep a risk line below 160, since a monthly close under that would tell me the trend is changing. On the upside, I need price to recover above 220 before I think about a retest of the high. Volume has been shrinking during this pullback, which suggests the selling isn't panic, but I still want to see buyers return. NVIDIA is the stock most tied to this month's catalysts. The Fed's November FOMC matters for high-growth valuations, the midterm elections could stir up headlines on chip exports and trade policy, and the late Q3 earnings season will show whether AI spending from big tech is still accelerating. Since many large companies have already reported, their spending plans will shape how I see NVIDIA from here. Great trends can still take long breaks, so I'm letting price show me where demand returns. Are you buying this dip in NVDA or waiting for a deeper pullback?
